candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The Nusselt number (Nu) is a dimensionless quantity representing the ratio of convective to conductive heat transfer across a fluid layer. It is derived from the given physical quantities related to Rayleigh-Bénard convection, which include length (h), temperature difference (delta_T), thermal conductivity (lambda), gravitational acceleration (g), thermal expansion coefficient (alpha), kinematic viscosity (nu), and thermal diffusivity (kappa). Each input's physical dimension is identified based on standard SI base units and physical definitions.

variables.physical_definition: height of the container, a length scale
temperature difference between the top and bottom surfaces
thermal conductivity, the rate of heat transfer through a material per unit area per unit temperature gradient
gravitational acceleration, acceleration due to gravity
thermal expansion coefficient, fractional change in volume per unit temperature change
kinematic viscosity, ratio of dynamic viscosity to density
thermal diffusivity, ratio of thermal conductivity to volumetric heat capacity

Its si_dimension is L (dimension_vector [0,1,0,0,0,0,0]), which directly supplies the length-only exponents expected for the problem's geometric height h. This record therefore justifies the candidate's pure L^1 assignment in the original Rayleigh-Bénard context.

The record pq_temperature_difference is the canonical entry for a temperature difference (symbols ΔT, delta_T) and is explicitly defined as the difference between two thermodynamic temperatures. Its si_dimension is Theta (dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,1,0,0]), which supports the candidate's single nonzero Theta^1 coordinate. This record applies because the problem input is the temperature difference between top and bottom surfaces.

The record pq_thermal_conductivity is the canonical thermal conductivity entry (symbols λ, lambda) used in Fourier's law and heat-transfer contexts. It lists si_dimension M L T^-3 Theta^-1 (dimension_vector [1,1,-3,0,-1,0,0]), matching every known coordinate of the candidate. It applies here because the problem uses thermal conductivity of the fluid/plates as λ in the conductive heat-flux term.

The record pq_gravitational_acceleration defines acceleration due to gravity with si_dimension L T^-2 (dimension_vector [0,1,-2,0,0,0,0]) and the canonical symbol g. In Rayleigh-Bénard convection g provides the body-force scale entering buoyancy; thus this record justifies the candidate's L^1 T^-2 assignment.

The record pq_thermal_expansion_coefficient is the canonical entry for the (volumetric/linear) thermal expansion coefficient, symbol α/alpha, defined as fractional change per unit temperature and carrying dimension Theta^-1 (dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,-1,0,0]). In the Rayleigh-Bénard problem α multiplies temperature differences in the buoyancy term, so this record justifies the Theta^-1 exponent.

The record pq_kinematic_viscosity is the standard kinematic viscosity entry (symbol ν/nu) defined as dynamic viscosity divided by density, with si_dimension L^2 T^-1 (dimension_vector [0,2,-1,0,0,0,0]). In fluid mechanics (including Rayleigh-Bénard) ν is the momentum diffusivity parameter used in the viscous term; this matches the candidate's L^2 T^-1 coordinates.

The record pq_thermal_diffusivity is the canonical thermal diffusivity entry (symbols κ/kappa) with si_dimension L^2 T^-1 (dimension_vector [0,2,-1,0,0,0,0]). Thermal diffusivity is used in the heat equation for Rayleigh-Bénard convection, so this record supports the candidate's L^2 T^-1 assignment.
